summary.headline: A behind-target week for orders and revenue, with the quarter also short of target and the full-year pace behind what's required.

points.what: Orders were 942, down 2.8% WoW and at 93.6% of target.
points.so_what: Orders grew 70.3% YoY, below the 75% growth built into targets, consistent with the week landing under target.

points.what: Revenue was $67,610, down 8.7% WoW and at 90.2% of target.
points.so_what: Revenue's shortfall was larger than orders' shortfall, pointing to weaker average order value alongside fewer orders this week.

points.what: YTD revenue is 94.9% of target, with the required weekly run-rate of $83,789 above the current 8-week run-rate of $66,432.
points.so_what: At the current pace, the full-year revenue target is not on track to be reached.

points.what: Search, the largest traffic source at 66.6% share of orders, fell 8.3% WoW.
points.so_what: As the largest source of orders, Search's decline was the main driver of the week's overall order drop.

points.what: QTD revenue attainment is 97.7%, behind target by $15,299 with 3 weeks left in the quarter.
points.so_what: Reaching the full quarter target now depends on closing this shortfall in the remaining three weeks.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the week of May 18 rose to 11.4%, up 0.5pp WoW and up 0.8pp YoY.
points.so_what: Both comparisons moving in the same direction signals a return-rate risk that is not improving.

points.what: AOV fell to $84.72, down 5.8% WoW and down 3.7% YoY.
points.so_what: Falling on both comparisons shows the revenue shortfall reflects smaller order values, not only fewer orders.

points.what: Weekly orders were 93.6% of target and weekly revenue was 90.2% of target.
points.so_what: Both KPIs fell short of the weekly target, making this a behind-target week overall.

points.what: QTD revenue is 97.7% of target, a gap of $15,299 with 3 weeks left in the quarter.
points.so_what: Closing this gap now requires stronger revenue performance in the quarter's remaining weeks.

points.what: YTD revenue is 94.9% of target, with the required weekly run-rate of $83,789 above the current 8-week run-rate of $66,432.
points.so_what: At the current pace, the full-year revenue target is not on track to be reached.

points.what: EMEA orders fell 16.1% WoW, contributing -33 orders, the largest negative contributor to the week's order decline.
points.so_what: EMEA's drop outweighed gains elsewhere, pulling total orders below last week's level despite growth in APAC.

points.what: Search orders fell 8.3% WoW, contributing -57 orders while holding 66.6% share of total orders.
points.so_what: Given its size, Search's decline was the main driver of the week's overall order drop.

points.what: APAC orders rose 5.9% WoW, contributing +24 orders, the only region to grow this week.
points.so_what: APAC's growth partly offset declines elsewhere but was not enough to prevent the week's overall order drop.

points.what: Cancellation rate was 15.3%, up 0.3pp WoW but down 1.5pp YoY.
points.so_what: The rate moved higher than last week even though it's better than a year ago, a risk if the WoW rise continues.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the week of May 18 was 11.4%, up 0.5pp WoW and up 0.8pp YoY.
points.so_what: Rising on both comparisons means more orders are being returned than a year ago, a drag on realized revenue not reflected in gross revenue.

points.what: New signups were 236, down 5.6% WoW and down 6.3% YoY.
points.so_what: Signups falling YoY while orders grew 70.3% YoY shows order growth is not coming from new customer acquisition.

points.what: AOV was $84.72, down 5.8% WoW and down 3.7% YoY.
points.so_what: AOV falling on both comparisons means part of this week's revenue decline reflects smaller order values, not only fewer orders.

checks.name: 14-Day Return Rate names its mature week
anomaly flag acknowledged in the summary
sentences at most 30 words and 4 numbers
each slot only covers its allowed KPIs
